messages.subject: CC mice - adding sex as a covariate and CC078
messages.subject_clean: CC mice - adding sex as a covariate and CC078
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dr. Broman,

Hope you are doing well, I work with the Collaborative Cross (CC) Mice population. I have been using rqtl2 to run some of my data. I got all the files from
https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/blob/master/CC/cc.zip
Thanks for all the preprocessing and example files.

I have some questions.

1. I have been averaging  6 animals (3 males and 3 females) from each line to a single data point for the analysis, Is there a way to include sex as a covariate?  (i.e., to run them as CC001M and CC001F, instead of just CC001).
2. The raw data stops at CC076, I have some data from CC078. Is there a way to include the data from CC078 into the analysis ( If its simple enough, I can try to do it myself)? or is there a possibility that it will get added in the future?

I have attached my .josn file. I will appreciate any help on this.

Thank you,

messages.subject: Re: CC mice - adding sex as a covariate and CC078
messages.subject_clean: CC mice - adding sex as a covariate and CC078
messages.body_plain:
Regarding sex as a covariate, personally I would focus on the average of the two sexes and the difference between the sexes.

But if you want to do an analysis with sex as a covariate, you'd need to double the lines with changed names, as you suggest. It'd be particularly important to use an LMM with a kinship matrix, because the pairs CC001M and CC001F have identical genotypes.

There's not currently facilities for doing this double of lines' genotypes in R/qtl2, but I've written some related code for doing individual-level analysis in RILs that might be useful to you:

    https://gist.github.com/kbroman/e09f8116401180b80005d47d4358764f

Regarding the genotypes for CC078: you can try adding it to the existing data at https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data
You can see the scripts I used to create those data files in https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/tree/master/CC/R

I'd like to help folks to analyze CC data in R/qtl2 by making the genotype data available in an easy-to-use format. If you can recommend a source for additional CC data, I'd be happy to hear about it.

karl

messages.subject: zip_datafiles() not doing anything
messages.body_plain:
Hey Karl-

I've been using R/qtl2 to map qtls in the HS/Npt, a mouse heterogeneous stock. I did some analyses a little over two years ago and all seemed to work well. Recently I've reevaluated the genotype data (from the GigaMUGA array) and have begun using these data in a new analysis with the latest version of R/qtl2.  Strangely, when I invoke the zip_datafiles() command, nothing happens. No output and no error -- just nothing. I've tried it with the old dataset that worked before and with the new one -- same result. Any ideas? Below is the command I used and the yaml file.

>zip_datafiles("control_47593.yaml")

# YAML format
# This is the R/QTL2 control file for data files related to the Nicotine preference project.
# Population = HS/Npt
# Genotypes derived from the GigaMUGA array

crosstype: hs
geno: geno_47593.csv
geno_transposed: true
founder_geno: npt_geno_47593.csv
founder_geno_transposed: true
genotypes:
  A: 1
  H: 2
  B: 3
pheno: pheno_476_corrected.csv
pheno_transposed: false
covar: covar_476_corrected.csv
sex:
  covar: sex
  f: female
  m: male
x_chr: X
cross_info:
  covar: ngen
gmap: gmap_47593.csv
pmap: pmap_47593.csv
alleles:
- A
- B
- C
- D
- E
- F
- G
- H
na.strings:
- NA
- ‘-‘

messages.subject: Re: zip_datafiles() not doing anything
messages.body_plain:
What operating system are you using? And what version of R and R/qtl2.

Type R.version and qtl2::qtl2version().

If zip_datafiles() works, it won't produce any output but will create a zip file where that .yaml file is located.
It's not a very critical function; you could just go to that directory and zip the files directly yourself, but I'm surprised it's not working without giving some error message.

Maybe if you use quiet=FALSE when you call zip_datafiles(), it'll give some message about what's going wrong?

karl

messages.subject: Most appropriate cross type?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I am having trouble figuring out which, if any, cross type I should be using for my particular crossing design.
The individuals that I have phenotype/genotype data for are the progeny of intercrossed individuals from distinct RIL populations.
Starting from 4 inbred lines, I created three RIL populations. One inbred line (yellow in the attached image) was crossed to each of the three other inbred lines (shades of red in the attached image).  After these F1 lines were selfed to F6, individuals from different RIL populations were intercrossed. These F1s from crosses between RIL individuals is what I have genotyped/phenotyped.
So, there are four possible genotypes in an individual in each of these groups and 7 possible genotypes in the whole population.
Is there a cross type that would be compatible with this type of design?

Thank you!
Sam

messages.subject: Re: Most appropriate cross type?
messages.body_plain:
We don't really have a cross type that fits. There's nothing in R/qtl2 for RIX populations.

I would use the genotype data on the group 1, 2, and 3 RILs to get genotype probabilities for the parents of the RIX.
You could then combine those probabilities to get probabilities for the RIX population, but R/qtl2 doesn't currently have any facilities to help.

karl
